text: This capstone built one real integration end to end, across four lessons: an event-driven webhook triggered by Meridian HR, a REST Message pull authenticated with real OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials, and the production-grade retries, idempotency checks, and structured logging that keep it running when something inevitably goes wrong. This lesson closes it out the way a working developer actually would — with a written test plan, not just a hope that it keeps working after one clean manual run.

Five test cases matter here. A successful sync proves the happy path end to end. Meridian HR being unreachable proves retries actually fire with increasing delay before giving up cleanly. A malformed response proves a bad payload gets caught and logged instead of creating a garbage user. A redelivered webhook — the same employee ID twice — proves idempotency actually holds, not just in theory. And an expired OAuth token proves RESTMessageV2 refreshes it transparently, with no code change and no manual re-authentication.

A background script is the real way to prove idempotency instead of just assuming it holds: pull the same employee record once, create the pending user, then call that same create method again with identical data — simulating Meridian HR redelivering the exact same webhook notification a second time. If Lesson 28's idempotency check is actually working, both calls return the very same sys_id, and exactly one sys_user record exists afterward, not two.

This course closes a three-course stage in this path. JavaScript gave you the language itself — variables, functions, control flow. Scripting & Application Development gave you GlideRecord, Business Rules, and Script Includes — how ServiceNow's own data and automation actually run. IntegrationHub & REST APIs gave you everything needed to connect ServiceNow to the outside world — REST Messages, authentication, exposing your own data, and MID Servers. This capstone is where all three courses came together in one integration that genuinely works, start to finish.

Course 8 in this path, ServiceNow ITSM Implementation, is next — and it shifts focus entirely away from building integrations toward implementing full incident, problem, and change management processes, using every scripting and integration skill this three-course Application Development stage just built.
